Creating levels usually has many obstacles, especially with motivation, even if you are passionate about the level. Normally the only reward is simply finishing the project. However, if creators can work with the same passion and also get paid, they gain an additional goal. Instead of just completing the level, they also receive financial rewards for their hard work. This means the reward is not only the feeling of accomplishment but also money that can be used in real life, such as upgrading devices or buying design/art courses, which ultimately helps the creator improve.
2:32 PM
Another factor is age. As creators grow older, they face more responsibilities in life, which leaves them with less time or reason to continue creating even if their passion remains the same. In this context, money can help offset those responsibilities. Financial rewards can compensate for the time and energy spent creating the level, allowing creators to justify continuing their work despite other obligations.

Arkonix 3/5/2026 4:15 PM
I get why people have their issues with it, especially because of the money, the marketing and the fact that it’s based on an already existing level. But at the end of the day there are still real people building this, putting in hours of work and creativity. Just because a lot of money is involved doesn’t mean there’s no passion behind it. Some say it feels greedy, and I understand why it might look like that from the outside. But isn’t earning money something most people aim for in life? If someone manages to combine their passion with making money, that’s not automatically a bad thing. Nobody is forced to buy anything, it’s still a personal choice. Yes, it’s not 100 percent original. But the original level had insane hype and clearly left an impact. Expanding something that already had huge potential isn’t a terrible idea in my opinion. A lot of successful projects are inspired by or built on existing concepts, that’s just how creative industries work. Also people underestimate how much time and effort goes into an 8 minute megacollab. Coordinating creators, building, testing, polishing everything, that takes a lot. Paying creators can also be seen as respecting their time instead of expecting free labor. In the end I just think we should wait until it’s fully released before judging too harshly. It might not be perfect and it might not be for everyone, but that doesn’t mean it’s pointless or soulless.

I still think it doesn’t deserve this much hate. The plushies are basically just merch, if someone wants one they can buy it, if not they can just ignore it. It’s not a scam, and the lootboxes aren’t really gambling since you can’t actually lose your money, you always receive something. Waboo might profit partly from the idea of extending the level, but the plushies themselves are based on new bosses that were created for the project and only inspired by Skeletal Shenanigans. For me the main point isn’t defending everything Waboo does or pretending it’s perfect. I just think the level extension itself looks cool and interesting, and the merch is more of a side thing. Personally I don’t even care about the merch that much, I’m mostly interested in seeing what the finished level will look like : )
